source.text: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.

en.L: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
en.B: They reached the far side of the lake, the country of the Gerasenes.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed Lake Galilee to the other side. They came to the land where the Gerasene people lived.

vi.L: Và họ đến bờ bên kia biển, vào vùng của người Giê-ra-sê.
vi.B: Họ đến bờ bên kia biển, vào vùng đất của người Giê-ra-sê.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi qua bờ bên kia hồ Ga-li-lê. Họ đến vùng đất của người Giê-ra-sê.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 바다 건너편, 거라사 사람들의 지방으로 갔다.
ko.B: 그들은 바다 건너편 거라사 사람들의 지방에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 제자들과 함께 갈릴리 호수를 건너 맞은편으로 가셨다. 그들은 거라사 사람들이 사는 땅에 도착했다.

es.L: Y llegaron al otro lado del mar, a la región de los gerasenos.
es.B: Llegaron a la otra orilla del mar, a la región de los gerasenos.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos cruzaron el lago de Galilea hasta la otra orilla. Llegaron a la tierra donde vivían los gerasenos.

fr.L: Et ils vinrent de l’autre côté de la mer, dans la région des Géraséniens.
fr.B: Ils arrivèrent sur l’autre rive de la mer, dans le pays des Géraséniens.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont traversé le lac de Galilée jusqu’à l’autre rive. Ils sont arrivés dans le pays où habitaient les Géraséniens.

sw.L: Na wakafika ng'ambo ya bahari, katika nchi ya Wagerasi.
sw.B: Walifika ng'ambo ya bahari, katika nchi ya Wagerasi.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walivuka Ziwa Galilaya mpaka upande wa pili. Wakafika katika nchi walimoishi watu wa Gerasi.

decisions.choice: Gerasenes, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ on the name. The earliest Alexandrian and Western witnesses have Gerasenes; many later manuscripts have Gadarenes, the name in Matthew 8:28; some have Gergesenes. Gerasa and Gadara were towns of the Decapolis some distance from the lake, and the name may refer to the wider district rather than the town itself. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the other side of the sea: the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: The crossing began in 4:35. The eastern shore was mostly Gentile country, which explains the herd of pigs (5:11).

decisions.choice: they came: Jesus and his disciples, who set out in 4:35-36
decisions.reason: The plural carries on from the storm on the lake. From 5:2 Mark follows Jesus alone.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers crossed Lake Galilee
alternatives: they came to the other side of the sea
decisions.reason: Readable names who is travelling and which lake it is.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L, B); "hồ Ga-li-lê", then "hồ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Gospel calls the large freshwater Lake of Galilee a "sea". As in the Vietnamese John (6:1, 6:16-25), Literal and Balanced keep "biển", the word readers know from the Gospels, and Readable says "hồ" so that new readers picture a lake. Used through Mark 5.

decisions.choice: "người Giê-ra-sê"
decisions.reason: The name follows the Protestant transliteration of the SBLGNT reading "Gerasenes" (meaning decision); the variant names are in the footnote.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("말한다", "말씀하신다", "온다"), through chapter 5
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (5:7, 5:9, 5:15, 5:19, 5:22-23, 5:35-36, 5:38-41); Balanced and Readable use the past. Recorded once for the chapter, as in the Korean Mark 3.

decisions.choice: "거라사 사람들" for the Gerasenes; "바다" (L, B), "갈릴리 호수" (R) for the sea
decisions.reason: "거라사" is the established Protestant form of the name (style guide, section 5). The Sea of Galilee stays "바다" at Literal and Balanced and is called a lake at Readable, as in the Korean Mark 3:7 and John 6:1.

decisions.choice: el mar (L, B); el lago (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "mar", the Greek word and the name Spanish readers know (as in 1:16); Readable says "lago", since this "sea" is the freshwater Lake of Galilee, so readers do not picture the ocean. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos ... el lago de Galilea
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names who crossed (4:35-36) and which lake. It keeps "discípulos", as the Spanish of John does at every level, where the English Readable says "followers"; this applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B) and the passé composé (R); Literal uses the passé simple too but keeps Mark’s present tense where he tells a past event in the present ("il dit", "ils viennent", 5:7, 15, 19, 22-23, 35-41); the imperfect at every level for what was going on
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for Mark 5. The passé simple ("ils vinrent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("ils sont arrivés"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Mark’s historic present is kept only at Literal, as in the English and as in the French John.

decisions.choice: la mer (L, B); le lac, le lac de Galilée (R)
alternatives: le lac (B), as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: As in the French of John (6:16) and of Mark 3-4: Literal and Balanced keep "la mer", the Greek word and the usual French name ("la mer de Galilée"); Readable says "le lac" so young readers do not picture the open sea (meaning decision m2). The same holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: bahari (L, B); Ziwa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Swahili of John 6, Literal and Balanced keep "bahari" (sea), the word Mark uses for the Sea of Galilee; Readable calls it what it is, "Ziwa Galilaya" (Lake Galilee), as the English Readable does. Used through Mark 5 and 6.

decisions.choice: Wagerasi (L, B); watu wa Gerasi (R)
decisions.reason: The people are named with the Swahili plural prefix wa-, as in "Wayahudi"; Readable says "the people of Gerasa" for new readers.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi wake; fewer deity_pronoun spans than English
decisions.reason: Swahili says "wanafunzi" (disciples) at every level, where the English Readable says "followers". Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb, where no capital is possible, so these chapters have spans only on free pronouns and possessives ("wake", "yake", "naye", "kwake").

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every separate pronoun for Jesus
decisions.reason: The rule for Mark set at 1:2: every pronoun Spanish writes for Jesus as a separate word (él, lo, le, su, sus, mí, mi, te, tu) carries the span; a pronoun at the start of a sentence, one joined to the end of a verb, and "conmigo", "contigo", "consigo" are written plain. This applies throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ, ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν, καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσι δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι·

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out of him out of the boat, immediately met him out of the tombs a man with a spirit unclean, \v 3 who the dwelling had in the tombs, and not even with a chain no longer anyone was able him to bind, \v 4 because him often with shackles and chains to have been bound, and to have been torn apart by him the chains and the shackles to have been shattered, and no one was strong enough him to subdue.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [coming] out of the tombs, \v 3 who had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one was able any longer to bind him, not even with a chain, \v 4 because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles shattered, and no one was strong enough to subdue him.
en.B: As soon as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came out from the tombs to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 3 This man lived among the tombs, and nobody could keep him tied up anymore, not even with a chain. \v 4 Time and again he had been bound hand and foot with irons and chains, but he had pulled the chains apart and smashed the irons on his feet. No one had the strength to control him.
en.R: Jesus got out of the boat. Right away a man came out from the burial caves to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The man had an evil spirit in him. \v 3 He lived in the burial caves. No one could tie him up anymore, not even with chains. \v 4 People had often put chains on his hands and feet. But he always broke the chains apart and smashed the metal rings on his feet. No one was strong enough to control him.

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vừa ra khỏi thuyền, lập tức từ các mộ có một người có linh ô uế đi ra gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 3 là người sống giữa các mộ, và không ai còn có thể trói anh ta được nữa, dù bằng xích cũng không, \v 4 vì anh ta đã nhiều lần bị cùm chân và xích lại, nhưng xích đã bị anh ta bứt đứt và cùm bị đập vỡ, và không ai đủ sức chế ngự anh ta.
vi.B: Ngài vừa bước ra khỏi thuyền thì có một người bị linh ô uế ám từ các mộ đi ra gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 3 Người này sống giữa các mộ, và không ai còn trói được anh ta nữa, ngay cả bằng xích. \v 4 Đã nhiều lần anh ta bị cùm chân và xích tay, nhưng anh ta bứt đứt xích và đập vỡ cùm. Không ai đủ sức chế ngự anh ta.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu vừa ra khỏi thuyền thì ngay lập tức có một người từ các hang mộ đi ra gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Người này bị tà linh ám. \v 3 Anh ta sống trong các hang mộ. Không ai còn trói được anh ta nữa, kể cả bằng xích sắt. \v 4 Người ta đã nhiều lần lấy xích trói tay và lấy cùm cùm chân anh ta. Nhưng lần nào anh ta cũng bứt đứt xích và đập vỡ cùm sắt ở chân. Không ai đủ sức khống chế anh ta.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 배에서 내리시자, 곧 더러운 영이 들린 한 사람이 무덤들 사이에서 [나와] 그분을 맞았다. \v 3 그는 무덤들 사이에 거처를 두고 있었는데, 이제는 아무도 쇠사슬로조차 그를 묶어 둘 수 없었다. \v 4 그가 여러 번 족쇄와 쇠사슬에 묶였지만, 쇠사슬은 그에게 끊어지고 족쇄는 부서졌기 때문이다. 그리고 아무도 그를 길들일 만큼 힘이 세지 못했다.
ko.B: 예수께서 배에서 내리시자 곧바로, 더러운 영이 들린 사람 하나가 무덤 사이에서 나와 예수를 맞았다. \v 3 그 사람은 무덤 사이에서 살았는데, 이제는 아무도 그를 묶어 둘 수 없었다. 쇠사슬로도 소용이 없었다. \v 4 사람들이 여러 번 그의 손발을 족쇄와 쇠사슬로 묶어 두었지만, 그는 쇠사슬을 끊고 족쇄를 깨뜨려 버렸다. 아무도 그를 휘어잡을 힘이 없었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 배에서 내리셨다. 바로 그때 어떤 사람이 무덤 동굴에서 나와 예수를 만났다. 그 사람에게는 악한 영이 들어 있었다. \v 3 그는 무덤 동굴에서 살았다. 이제는 아무도 그를 묶어 둘 수 없었다. 쇠사슬로도 안 되었다. \v 4 사람들이 여러 번 그의 손과 발을 쇠사슬로 묶어 두었다. 그러나 그는 그때마다 쇠사슬을 끊고, 발에 채운 쇠고랑을 부수어 버렸다. 아무도 그를 당해 낼 수 없었다.

es.L: Y al salir {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de la barca, enseguida vino a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro desde los sepulcros un hombre con un espíritu impuro, \v 3 que tenía su morada en los sepulcros; y ya nadie podía atarlo, ni siquiera con una cadena, \v 4 porque muchas veces había sido atado con grilletes y cadenas, y él había roto las cadenas y destrozado los grilletes, y nadie tenía fuerza para dominarlo.
es.B: En cuanto Jesús bajó de la barca, un hombre con un espíritu impuro salió de entre los sepulcros a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. \v 3 Este hombre vivía en los sepulcros, y ya nadie podía tenerlo atado, ni siquiera con cadenas. \v 4 Muchas veces lo habían sujetado de pies y manos con grilletes y cadenas, pero él rompía las cadenas y hacía pedazos los grilletes. Nadie tenía fuerza para dominarlo.
es.R: Jesús bajó de la barca. Enseguida un hombre salió de las cuevas de los sepulcros y fue a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. Ese hombre tenía dentro un espíritu maligno. \v 3 Vivía en las cuevas de los sepulcros. Ya nadie podía tenerlo atado, ni siquiera con cadenas. \v 4 Muchas veces le habían puesto cadenas en las manos y en los pies. Pero él siempre rompía las cadenas y hacía pedazos los grilletes de los pies. Nadie tenía fuerza para controlarlo.

fr.L: Et lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut sorti de la barque, aussitôt un homme avec un esprit impur vint à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre, [sortant] des tombeaux, \v 3 lequel avait sa demeure dans les tombeaux ; et personne ne pouvait plus le lier, pas même avec une chaîne, \v 4 parce qu’il avait souvent été lié avec des entraves et des chaînes, et que les chaînes avaient été rompues par lui et les entraves brisées ; et personne n’avait la force de le dompter.
fr.B: Dès qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut descendu de la barque, un homme possédé par un esprit impur sortit des tombeaux et vint à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. \v 3 Cet homme vivait dans les tombeaux, et personne ne parvenait plus à le tenir attaché, même avec une chaîne. \v 4 Bien des fois, on lui avait mis des fers aux pieds et des chaînes, mais il avait arraché les chaînes et brisé les fers. Personne n’avait la force de le maîtriser.
fr.R: Jésus est descendu de la barque. Tout de suite, un homme est sorti des grottes où l’on enterrait les morts, et il est venu vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Cet homme avait en lui un esprit mauvais. \v 3 Il habitait dans ces grottes. Personne ne pouvait plus l’attacher, même avec des chaînes. \v 4 Souvent, on lui avait mis des chaînes aux mains et aux pieds. Mais chaque fois, il cassait les chaînes et il brisait les anneaux de fer de ses pieds. Personne n’était assez fort pour le maîtriser.

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kutoka katika mashua, mara moja mtu mwenye roho mchafu alikutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} [akitoka] makaburini, \v 3 ambaye makao yake yalikuwa makaburini, na hakuna mtu aliyeweza tena kumfunga, hata kwa mnyororo, \v 4 kwa sababu mara nyingi alikuwa amefungwa kwa pingu na minyororo, na minyororo ilikuwa imekatwa-katwa naye na pingu zimevunjwa-vunjwa, na hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na nguvu za kumdhibiti.
sw.B: Mara tu Yesu aliposhuka kutoka mashuani, mtu mwenye roho mchafu alitoka makaburini akaja kukutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. \v 3 Mtu huyo aliishi makaburini, na hakuna mtu aliyeweza kumfunga tena, hata kwa mnyororo. \v 4 Mara nyingi alikuwa amefungwa kwa minyororo na kwa pingu za miguu, lakini aliikata-kata minyororo na kuzivunja pingu. Hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na nguvu za kumdhibiti.
sw.R: Yesu alishuka kutoka kwenye mashua. Mara hiyo mtu mmoja alitoka kwenye mapango ya makaburi akaja kukutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Mtu huyo alikuwa na roho mwovu ndani yake. \v 3 Aliishi kwenye mapango hayo ya makaburi. Hakuna mtu aliyeweza kumfunga tena, hata kwa minyororo. \v 4 Mara nyingi watu walikuwa wamemfunga minyororo mikononi na miguuni. Lakini kila mara aliikata minyororo hiyo na kuvunja pingu za miguu yake. Hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na nguvu za kumdhibiti.

decisions.choice: the tombs: burial caves cut in the hillside
decisions.reason: Tombs in that region were often caves or rooms cut into rock, where a person could shelter. To live among the dead made a person unclean in Jewish law (Numbers 19:11-16).

decisions.choice: not even with a chain, no longer, no one: a string of negatives for emphasis
alternatives: a weaker statement that binding was hard
decisions.reason: Greek piles up negatives to make the point stronger: nothing at all could hold him any more.

decisions.choice: shackles: fetters for the feet
decisions.reason: The word is used for chains or irons on the feet, set beside chains, which could bind the hands.

decisions.choice: subdue: tame, as one tames a wild animal
decisions.reason: The verb is used for taming animals (James 3:7). The man is pictured as wild and beyond human control.

decisions.choice: burial caves
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of tombs a man could live in.

decisions.choice: the long clause is split into separate sentences
alternatives: one sentence with a chain of infinitives
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the sentence where the Greek gives the reason, to keep it readable.

decisions.choice: "linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R)
decisions.reason: "Linh" in lowercase is the style guide's word for a spirit that is not the Holy Spirit, and "ô uế" keeps Mark's word "unclean", which ties the spirits to the law's clean and unclean. "Thần ô uế" is the Catholic form. Readable says "tà linh" (evil spirit), the plain word, as the English Readable says "evil spirit". Used through Mark 5.

decisions.choice: "anh ta" for the man
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose a pronoun that marks age and attitude. "Anh ta" is neutral for a man of unknown age; "hắn" would make the narrator despise him.

decisions.choice: "곧" (L); "곧바로" (B); "바로" (R) for euthys, through chapter 5
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 3: Mark's frequent "immediately" keeps one Korean word per level so the pace of his telling stays visible; "즉시" sounds administrative in narrative.

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R); "족쇄" for the shackles; "길들이다" (L) for subdue
decisions.reason: "더러운 영" keeps Mark's word "unclean" and Readable says "악한 영", as in the Korean Mark 3:11. "족쇄" is the everyday word for fetters on the feet; "차꼬" is old. Literal keeps the picture of taming a wild animal (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say that no one could hold him down.

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: "Impuro" says in plain modern Spanish what the Greek adjective says: the spirit makes a person unclean before God. "Inmundo" is the older word. As in English, Readable says "maligno", which young readers understand. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: enseguida (L); en cuanto (B); Enseguida (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's frequent "immediately": Literal always says "enseguida"; Balanced and Readable use whatever Spanish phrase fits the sentence ("en cuanto", "al instante", "enseguida"). This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: las cuevas de los sepulcros
decisions.reason: As in English: the tombs were burial caves cut in the hillside (meaning decision), which Readable says plainly.

decisions.choice: esprit impur (L, B); esprit mauvais (R)
decisions.reason: "Esprit impur" keeps the Greek word, which ties these spirits to what the law calls unclean (the pigs in 5:11-13). Readable says "esprit mauvais", as the English Readable says "evil spirit"; "mauvais esprit" is avoided because in everyday French it means a bad attitude. The same choice holds throughout Mark 5.

decisions.choice: aussitôt (L); dès que (B); tout de suite (R)
decisions.reason: Mark’s frequent "immediately" is "aussitôt" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say it in the way that suits each sentence ("dès que", "aussitôt", "à l’instant même", "tout de suite"). This holds for the chapter.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Jesus or for God takes the deity_pronoun setting, including the object pronouns and possessives French needs where English has none ("vint à sa rencontre"); a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: roho mchafu (L, B); roho mwovu (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps Mark's two words apart: "roho" for the spirit (pneuma) and "pepo" for the demon (daimonion, 5:15). "Mchafu" (unclean, impure) keeps the sense of ritual uncleanness. "Roho" takes personal agreement here (mchafu, wachafu, roho hao), because the spirits act and speak as beings. Readable says "roho mwovu" (evil spirit), as the English Readable does. For the whole of Mark.

decisions.choice: mara moja (L, B); mara hiyo, mara tu (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's frequent "immediately" (euthys) is "mara moja" at Literal and Balanced, so the reader sees how often Mark uses it; Readable uses the plainer "mara hiyo" or folds it into the sentence.

source.text: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.

records.literal_gloss: And constantly night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

en.L: And constantly, night and day, among the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
en.B: Night and day, without stopping, he would scream among the tombs and on the hills and slash himself with stones.
en.R: All night and all day he was in the burial caves and in the hills. He kept screaming and cutting himself with sharp stones.

vi.L: Và suốt đêm ngày, ở giữa các mộ và trên các núi, anh ta cứ kêu la và lấy đá cắt mình.
vi.B: Ngày đêm không ngớt, anh ta la hét giữa các mộ và trên các đồi, và lấy đá rạch mình.
vi.R: Suốt đêm suốt ngày, anh ta ở trong các hang mộ và trên các ngọn đồi. Anh ta cứ la hét và lấy đá nhọn cứa vào người mình.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 밤낮 늘 무덤들 사이와 산에서 소리를 지르며 돌로 자기 몸을 상하게 하고 있었다.
ko.B: 그는 밤낮 쉬지 않고 무덤 사이와 산에서 소리를 지르며, 돌로 제 몸에 상처를 냈다.
ko.R: 그는 밤에도 낮에도 무덤 동굴과 산속에서 지냈다. 그는 쉬지 않고 소리를 지르며, 날카로운 돌로 자기 몸을 그어 상처를 냈다.

es.L: Y continuamente, de noche y de día, en los sepulcros y en los montes, estaba gritando e hiriéndose con piedras.
es.B: Noche y día, sin parar, andaba gritando entre los sepulcros y por los montes, y se hacía cortes con piedras.
es.R: Día y noche estaba en las cuevas de los sepulcros y en los cerros. Gritaba sin parar y se cortaba con piedras afiladas.

fr.L: Et constamment, nuit et jour, dans les tombeaux et dans les montagnes, il criait et se lacérait avec des pierres.
fr.B: Nuit et jour, sans relâche, il hurlait parmi les tombeaux et sur les collines, et il se tailladait avec des pierres.
fr.R: Toute la nuit et toute la journée, il restait dans les grottes et dans les collines. Il criait sans arrêt et il se blessait avec des pierres coupantes.

sw.L: Na siku zote, usiku na mchana, makaburini na milimani alikuwa akipiga kelele na kujikatakata kwa mawe.
sw.B: Usiku na mchana, bila kukoma, alikuwa akipiga makelele makaburini na vilimani, na kujichanja-chanja kwa mawe.
sw.R: Usiku na mchana alikuwa kwenye mapango ya makaburi na vilimani. Aliendelea kupiga kelele na kujikata kwa mawe makali.

decisions.choice: he was crying out and cutting: an ongoing state
decisions.reason: The verb with participles describes what he kept doing, day after day.

decisions.choice: cutting: gashing, wounding
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut or gash. The spirit drives the man to harm himself.

decisions.choice: the mountains: the hills around the lake
decisions.reason: The word covers hill country as well as high mountains.

decisions.choice: les montagnes (L); les collines (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "les collines", the hills around the lake (meaning decision m3), as the French John does at Readable.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν, καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου;

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him, \v 7 and having cried out with a voice loud, he says, What to me and to you, Jesus, Son of the God the Most High?

en.L: And seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 7 and crying out with a loud voice, he says, "What [is there] to me and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?
en.B: When he caught sight of Jesus a long way off, he ran up and threw himself down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 7 He gave a loud shriek: "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, what have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do with me?
en.R: The man saw Jesus far away. He ran to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and got down on his knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 7 He shouted very loudly, "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering me?

vi.L: Và thấy Đức Giê-xu từ xa, anh ta chạy đến và quỳ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 7 rồi kêu lớn tiếng, anh ta nói: "[Có việc] gì giữa tôi với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, hỡi Đức Giê-xu, Con Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao?
vi.B: Vừa trông thấy Đức Giê-xu từ đằng xa, anh ta chạy đến, sấp mình xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 7 và thét lớn: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, Con Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn gì với tôi?
vi.R: Người ấy thấy Đức Giê-xu từ xa. Anh ta chạy đến và quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 7 Anh ta hét thật lớn: "Hỡi Đức Giê-xu, Con Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao! Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại đến quấy rầy tôi?

ko.L: 그리고 그가 멀리서 예수를 보고 달려와서 그분께 엎드려 절했다. \v 7 그리고 큰 소리로 외치며 말한다. "나와 당신에게 무엇이 [있습니까], 지극히 높으신 하나님의 아들 예수님?
ko.B: 그는 멀리서 예수를 보자 달려와서 그 앞에 엎드렸다. \v 7 그리고 큰 소리로 부르짖었다. "지극히 높으신 하나님의 아들 예수님, 당신이 나에게 무슨 볼일이 있습니까?
ko.R: 그 사람은 멀리서 예수를 보았다. 그는 예수께 달려가서 그 앞에 무릎을 꿇었다. \v 7 그리고 아주 큰 소리로 외쳤다. "지극히 높으신 하나님의 아들 예수님, 왜 나를 가만두지 않습니까?

es.L: Y al ver a Jesús desde lejos, corrió y se postró ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \v 7 y gritando con gran voz, dice: «¿Qué [hay] entre {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} y yo, Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo?
es.B: Cuando vio a Jesús desde lejos, corrió y se arrojó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies. \v 7 Dio un alarido: «Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo, ¿qué tienes que ver conmigo?
es.R: El hombre vio a Jesús a lo lejos. Corrió hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y se arrodilló delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 7 Gritó con todas sus fuerzas: «Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo, ¿por qué te metes conmigo?

fr.L: Et voyant Jésus de loin, il courut et se prosterna devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \v 7 et criant d’une voix forte, il dit : « Quoi [de commun] entre moi et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Jésus, Fils du Dieu Très-Haut ?
fr.B: Apercevant Jésus de loin, il accourut et se jeta à genoux devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \v 7 Il poussa un grand cri : « Jésus, Fils du Dieu Très-Haut, que me veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ?
fr.R: L’homme a vu Jésus de loin. Il a couru vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et s’est mis à genoux devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \v 7 Il a crié très fort : « Jésus, Fils du Dieu Très-Haut, qu’est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me veux ?

sw.L: Na alipomwona Yesu kwa mbali, alikimbia akamsujudia, \v 7 na akipiga kelele kwa sauti kuu, anasema, "Mimi na {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} tuna nini [pamoja], Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa?
sw.B: Alipomwona Yesu kwa mbali, alikimbia akaja akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 7 Akapiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, "Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, una shughuli gani nami?
sw.R: Mtu huyo alimwona Yesu akiwa mbali. Akakimbia, akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 7 Akapiga kelele kwa nguvu, "Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, kwa nini unanisumbua?

decisions.choice: bowed down: fell to his knees in homage
decisions.reason: The verb is used for kneeling before a king or a god. Here the spirit is forced to bow before one stronger than itself (3:11), not to trust in him.

decisions.choice: what to me and to you: what do we have in common? leave me alone
decisions.reason: As in 1:24, the phrase keeps someone at a distance and is hostile here.

decisions.choice: Son of the Most High God: the spirit knows who Jesus is
alternatives: a title the man had heard from others
decisions.reason: "Most High" is an old name for the God of Israel (Genesis 14:18-20) used also by non-Jews (Acts 16:17). The unclean spirits know Jesus as the Son of God (1:24; 3:11).

decisions.choice: he says: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The same is true of the presents through this chapter.

decisions.choice: said, shouted
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense, which English uses for telling a story.

decisions.choice: why are you bothering me?
alternatives: what to me and to you?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom.

decisions.choice: "tôi" and "ngài" (with the deity_pronoun setting) in the spirit's words
decisions.reason: The man speaks for the spirit, which knows who Jesus is and is afraid of him (meaning decisions). Vietnamese must choose a pronoun: "ông" would be too familiar for one who falls down before Jesus, and "Thầy" is what disciples say. "Ngài", the pronoun of fearful respect, carries the setting like the narrator's "ngài" (lowercase by default, as in ordinary writing). A reviewer may prefer "ông".

decisions.choice: "nói", "đến", "thấy" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present ("he says", 5:7, 5:9, 5:15, 5:22, 5:35-41). Vietnamese verbs have no tense, so Literal keeps the vividness by leaving out "đã"; Balanced and Readable narrate plainly. As in the Vietnamese John.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao"
decisions.reason: "Chí Cao" (most high) is the standing title for God in Vietnamese and keeps the Greek's superlative; it is capitalised as part of the title.

decisions.choice: The spirit speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "당신" and "예수님", and of itself as "나"
alternatives: the plain style for a hostile spirit
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 3:11, the spirit bows and names Jesus truly, so it speaks up to him; "당신" keeps the stressed "you" of the Greek, and "나" (not the humble "저") keeps its defiance. A reviewer may prefer another level for a hostile spirit.

decisions.choice: "당신이 나에게 무슨 볼일이 있습니까?" (B); "왜 나를 가만두지 않습니까?" (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom means "leave me alone" (meaning decision). Balanced says it with a modern question rather than the wording of familiar versions; Readable says what the spirit wants, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John: Literal keeps Mark's storytelling present ("dice", "vienen"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué [hay] entre tú y yo? (L); ¿qué tienes que ver conmigo? (B); ¿por qué te metes conmigo? (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom pushes Jesus away (meaning decision). Literal keeps its shape with one supplied word; Balanced uses the Spanish idiom that does the same; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: Quoi [de commun] entre moi et toi (L); que me veux-tu ? (B); qu’est-ce que tu me veux ? (R)
alternatives: Qu’y a-t-il entre moi et toi ? (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew-style idiom asks what the two have in common and means "leave me alone" (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the shape and brackets the word French needs; Balanced and Readable use the everyday French question "que me veux-tu ?", which carries the same hostile sense.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anasema); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the Swahili of John: Literal keeps the Greek present of past events ("anasema", "wanakuja"), and Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past with -li- and -ka-. This holds for Mark 5 and 6.

decisions.choice: Mimi na wewe tuna nini [pamoja] (L); una shughuli gani nami? (B)
decisions.reason: The idiom asks what the two have in common, that is, "leave me alone". Literal keeps both persons of the Greek; Balanced uses the everyday Swahili "una shughuli gani nami?" (what business do you have with me?).

decisions.choice: Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa
decisions.reason: The same title for God as in the Swahili of Hebrews 7:1.

source.text: ὁρκίζω σε τὸν θεόν, μή με βασανίσῃς.

records.literal_gloss: I adjure you by the God, not me torment.

en.L: I adjure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} by God, do not torment me!"
en.B: I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, with God as witness, do not torture me!"
en.R: Promise me in God's name that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not hurt me!"

vi.L: Tôi nhân danh Đức Chúa Trời buộc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: đừng hành hạ tôi!"
vi.B: Có Đức Chúa Trời chứng giám, tôi van xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đừng hành hạ tôi!"
vi.R: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hứa trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời là sẽ không làm khổ tôi!"

ko.L: 하나님을 두고 당신께 맹세를 요구합니다. 나를 괴롭히지 마십시오!"
ko.B: 하나님 앞에서 당신께 간청합니다. 나에게 고통을 주지 마십시오!"
ko.R: 나를 괴롭히지 않겠다고 하나님의 이름으로 약속해 주십시오!"

es.L: Te conjuro por Dios: ¡no me atormentes!».
es.B: Te lo suplico por Dios: ¡no me tortures!».
es.R: ¡Prométeme por Dios que no me vas a hacer daño!».

fr.L: Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}adjure par Dieu, ne me tourmente pas ! »
fr.B: Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en conjure par Dieu, ne me torture pas ! »
fr.R: Promets-moi devant Dieu que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne vas pas me faire de mal ! »

sw.L: Nakuapisha kwa Mungu, usinitese!"
sw.B: Nakusihi, Mungu akiwa shahidi, usinitese!"
sw.R: Niahidi kwa jina la Mungu kwamba hutaniumiza!"

decisions.choice: I adjure you: I put you under oath
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone swear by God. It is the language used to drive out spirits, here turned against Jesus.

decisions.choice: torment: punish, torture
decisions.reason: The spirits expect punishment at the judgment (Matthew 8:29). The verb is used for torture and for punishment.

decisions.choice: I beg you, with God as witness (B); Promise me in God's name (R)
decisions.reason: "Adjure" is rare in modern English. Balanced and Readable say what the oath formula means.

decisions.choice: "하나님을 두고 맹세를 요구합니다" (L); "하나님 앞에서 간청합니다" (B); "하나님의 이름으로 약속해 주십시오" (R)
decisions.reason: Adjure means to put someone under oath (meaning decision). Literal says that plainly; Balanced keeps the solemn appeal with God as witness; Readable turns it into the promise the spirit asks for.

decisions.choice: te conjuro por Dios (L); te lo suplico por Dios (B); prométeme por Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The verb puts someone under oath (meaning decision). Literal keeps the formal "conjurar"; Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: adjurer (L); conjurer (B)
decisions.reason: "Adjurer" is the exact word for putting someone under oath (meaning decision m1) but is rare; Balanced says "je t’en conjure par Dieu", the familiar French way of begging someone in God’s name, which keeps the oath.

source.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying for to him, Come out, the spirit the unclean, out of the man.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been saying to him, "Come out of the man, unclean spirit!"
en.B: This was because Jesus had been telling it, "Unclean spirit, come out of this man!"
en.R: The man said this because Jesus was already telling the evil spirit, "Get out of this man, evil spirit!"

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với anh ta: "Hỡi linh ô uế, hãy ra khỏi người này!"
vi.B: Ấy là vì Đức Giê-xu đã bảo nó: "Linh ô uế kia, hãy ra khỏi người này!"
vi.R: Người ấy nói vậy vì Đức Giê-xu đã ra lệnh cho tà linh: "Tà linh kia, hãy ra khỏi người này!"

ko.L: 그분이 그에게 "더러운 영아, 그 사람에게서 나오너라" 하고 말씀하고 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이미 "더러운 영아, 이 사람에게서 나오너라!" 하고 명령하고 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그 사람이 이렇게 말한 것은, 예수께서 이미 악한 영에게 "악한 영아, 이 사람에게서 나가라!" 하고 말씀하고 계셨기 때문이다.

es.L: Porque le decía: «¡Sal del hombre, espíritu impuro!».
es.B: Es que Jesús le estaba diciendo: «¡Espíritu impuro, sal de este hombre!».
es.R: El hombre dijo esto porque Jesús ya le estaba ordenando al espíritu: «¡Espíritu maligno, sal de este hombre!».

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui disait : « Sors de l’homme, esprit impur ! »
fr.B: C’est que Jésus lui disait : « Esprit impur, sors de cet homme ! »
fr.R: L’homme a dit cela parce que Jésus était déjà en train de dire à l’esprit : « Esprit mauvais, sors de cet homme ! »

sw.L: Kwa maana alikuwa akimwambia, "Toka, roho mchafu, katika mtu huyu!"
sw.B: Alisema hivyo kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa akimwambia, "Roho mchafu, mtoke mtu huyu!"
sw.R: Mtu huyo alisema hivyo kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa tayari amemwambia roho mwovu, "Wewe roho mwovu, mtoke mtu huyu!"

decisions.choice: for he had been saying: the reason for the spirit's outcry
decisions.reason: Mark explains afterwards what had already happened. The verb can mean that Jesus had begun to command it, or was commanding it while the spirit cried out.

decisions.choice: the unclean spirit: Jesus speaks to the spirit, not the man
alternatives: the man is told to leave
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to the spirit, which is to leave the man.

decisions.choice: This was because (B); The man said this because (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "for" explains.

decisions.choice: "nó" (B); "tà linh" (R) for "him"
decisions.reason: The Greek "him" could be the man or the spirit; the words that follow are spoken to the spirit (meaning decision). Literal keeps "anh ta" for the Greek pronoun; Balanced uses "nó", the pronoun for a spirit, and Readable names it.

decisions.choice: Es que Jesús (B); El hombre dijo esto porque Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: names Jesus and shows that "for" gives the reason for the outcry (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: il lui disait (imperfect)
decisions.reason: The imperfect says that Jesus had already begun to command the spirit and was still doing so when it cried out (meaning decision m1); French "disait" carries this without the pluperfect.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Τί ὄνομά σοι;

records.literal_gloss: And he was asking him, What name to you?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asking him, "What [is] your name?"
en.B: Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?"
en.R: Then Jesus asked, "What is your name?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi anh ta: "Tên của anh là gì?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu hỏi anh ta: "Anh tên là gì?"
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu hỏi: "Anh tên gì?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그에게 묻고 계셨다. "네 이름이 무엇이냐?"
ko.B: 그러자 예수께서 그에게 물으셨다. "네 이름이 무엇이냐?"
ko.R: 그러자 예수께서 물으셨다. "네 이름이 무엇이냐?"

es.L: Y le preguntaba: «¿Cuál [es] tu nombre?».
es.B: Entonces Jesús le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui demandait : « Quel [est] ton nom ? »
fr.B: Jésus lui demanda alors : « Quel est ton nom ? »
fr.R: Alors Jésus a demandé : « Comment t’appelles-tu ? »

sw.L: Na alikuwa akimwuliza, "Jina lako [ni] nani?"
sw.B: Kisha Yesu akamwuliza, "Jina lako ni nani?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akamwuliza, "Jina lako ni nani?"

decisions.choice: him, your: addressed to the man, but the spirit answers
decisions.reason: The reply in 5:9 shows the spirits speaking through him.

decisions.choice: what is your name: knowing a spirit's name was thought to give power over it
decisions.reason: Jesus does not need a name to drive out spirits, but the answer shows how many hold the man.

decisions.choice: Jesus says "anh" to the man
decisions.reason: The question is put to the man (meaning decision). "Anh" is the ordinary respectful word for a grown man of unknown age; "ngươi" sounds archaic and harsh.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι, ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν·

records.literal_gloss: And he says to him, Legion name to me, because many we are.

en.L: And he says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Legion [is] my name, because we are many."
en.B: He answered, "My name is Legion, since there are many of us."
en.R: He answered, "My name is Legion, because there are so many of us."

vi.L: Và anh ta nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tên tôi là Quân Đoàn, vì chúng tôi đông lắm."
vi.B: Anh ta trả lời: "Tên tôi là Quân Đoàn, vì chúng tôi rất đông."
vi.R: Anh ta đáp: "Tên tôi là Quân Đoàn, vì chúng tôi nhiều lắm."

ko.L: 그러자 그가 그분께 말한다. "내 이름은 레기온입니다. 우리가 많기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 그가 대답했다. "내 이름은 레기온입니다. 우리 수가 많기 때문입니다."
ko.R: 그가 대답했다. "내 이름은 레기온, 곧 군대입니다. 우리 수가 아주 많기 때문입니다."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Legión [es] mi nombre, porque somos muchos».
es.B: Él respondió: «Me llamo Legión, porque somos muchos».
es.R: Él respondió: «Me llamo Legión, porque somos muchísimos».

fr.L: Et il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Légion [est] mon nom, car nous sommes nombreux. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « Mon nom est Légion, car nous sommes nombreux. »
fr.R: Il a répondu : « Je m’appelle Légion, parce que nous sommes très nombreux. »

sw.L: Naye anamwambia, "Jina langu [ni] Legioni, kwa sababu sisi tu wengi."
sw.B: Akamjibu, "Jina langu ni Legioni, kwa maana sisi ni wengi."
sw.R: Akajibu, "Jina langu ni Legioni, kwa sababu sisi ni wengi sana."

decisions.choice: Legion: a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers
alternatives: a vague word for a crowd
decisions.reason: A Roman legion had about 6,000 soldiers. The name says that a great many spirits hold the man, like an occupying army.

decisions.choice: my name ... we are many: the speaker shifts from one to many
decisions.reason: One voice speaks for many spirits. Mark keeps both singular and plural (5:10, 12).

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense and leave the pronoun out.

decisions.choice: "Quân Đoàn", capitalised as a name
decisions.reason: The Latin army word was understood by Mark's readers: a unit of several thousand soldiers (meaning decision). "Quân đoàn" is the Vietnamese word for such a unit, so the reader hears what the name means; a transliteration like "Lê-giôn" would hide it.

decisions.choice: "레기온" (L, B); "레기온, 곧 군대" (R)
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the Latin word, so Korean keeps it as a name; "군대" alone would hide that it is a Roman unit. Readable adds what the word means (meaning decision: an army unit of several thousand).

decisions.choice: Legioni
decisions.reason: The Latin army word is kept as the name, in Swahili spelling, at every level; the meaning note explains that a legion was a Roman unit of several thousand soldiers. "Jeshi" (army) would explain it but turn the name into a description.

source.text: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας.

records.literal_gloss: And he was begging him much that not them he would send out of the region.

en.L: And he begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} many times not to send them out of the region.
en.B: He kept pleading with Jesus not to send them away out of that country.
en.R: He begged Jesus again and again, "Do not send us away from this area!"

vi.L: Và anh ta nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhiều lần, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đừng đuổi chúng ra khỏi vùng ấy.
vi.B: Anh ta cứ van nài Đức Giê-xu đừng đuổi chúng ra khỏi vùng đất ấy.
vi.R: Anh ta cứ van xin Đức Giê-xu mãi: "Xin đừng đuổi chúng tôi ra khỏi vùng này!"

ko.L: 그리고 그는 자기들을 그 지방 밖으로 보내지 말아 달라고 그분께 간곡히 빌었다.
ko.B: 그는 자기들을 그 지방에서 쫓아내지 말아 달라고 예수께 거듭 애원했다.
ko.R: 그는 예수께 몇 번이나 빌었다. "우리를 이 지방에서 쫓아내지 마십시오!"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba mucho que no los enviara fuera de la región.
es.B: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaba a Jesús con insistencia que no los echara de aquella región.
es.R: Le rogaba a Jesús una y otra vez: «¡No nos eches de esta región!».

fr.L: Et il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliait beaucoup de ne pas les envoyer hors de la région.
fr.B: Et il ne cessait de supplier Jésus de ne pas les chasser hors du pays.
fr.R: Il a supplié Jésus plusieurs fois : « Ne nous envoie pas loin de cette région ! »

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akimsihi sana asiwapeleke nje ya nchi ile.
sw.B: Aliendelea kumsihi Yesu sana asiwafukuze kutoka katika nchi ile.
sw.R: Akamsihi Yesu tena na tena, "Usitufukuze kutoka eneo hili!"

decisions.choice: them: the spirits, though the man speaks
decisions.reason: The plural refers to the spirits, who speak through one voice.

decisions.choice: out of the region: away from the land where they dwelt
decisions.reason: Mark speaks of the region; Luke 8:31 has the abyss. The spirits want to stay where they are.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Do not send us away from this area!
alternatives: that he would not send them out of the region
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech, which is easier to follow.

source.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη·

records.literal_gloss: There was now there near the mountain a herd of pigs great feeding.

en.L: Now there was there near the mountain a great herd of pigs feeding.
en.B: A large herd of pigs happened to be grazing on the hillside nearby.
en.R: There was a big group of pigs eating on the hill close by.

vi.L: Bấy giờ ở đó, gần núi, có một bầy heo lớn đang ăn.
vi.B: Gần đó, trên sườn đồi, có một bầy heo rất lớn đang ăn.
vi.R: Trên ngọn đồi gần đó có một bầy heo rất đông đang kiếm ăn.

ko.L: 그런데 거기 산 가까이에 큰 돼지 떼가 먹이를 먹고 있었다.
ko.B: 마침 그 근처 산비탈에서 큰 돼지 떼가 먹이를 먹고 있었다.
ko.R: 가까운 산비탈에서 많은 돼지가 먹이를 먹고 있었다.

es.L: Había allí, junto al monte, una gran piara de cerdos paciendo.
es.B: Cerca de allí, en la ladera del monte, estaba paciendo una gran piara de cerdos.
es.R: Cerca de allí, en el cerro, había muchos cerdos comiendo.

fr.L: Or il y avait là, près de la montagne, un grand troupeau de porcs qui paissait.
fr.B: Or un grand troupeau de porcs paissait tout près, sur le flanc de la colline.
fr.R: Tout près, sur la colline, il y avait un grand troupeau de cochons qui mangeaient.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa huko karibu na mlima kundi kubwa la nguruwe likilisha.
sw.B: Kundi kubwa la nguruwe lilikuwa likilisha pale kando ya kilima.
sw.R: Karibu na hapo, kwenye kilima, kulikuwa na kundi kubwa la nguruwe likila.

decisions.choice: a herd of pigs: animals the law of Moses calls unclean
alternatives: farm animals of no special meaning
decisions.reason: Jews did not eat or keep pigs (Leviticus 11:7). A large herd shows that this was Gentile country.

decisions.choice: near the mountain: on the slope of the hill
alternatives: at the foot of a high mountain
decisions.reason: The herd is on the hillside above the lake, from which it rushes down (5:13).

decisions.choice: "heo"
decisions.reason: "Heo" (southern) and "lợn" (northern) are both standard. "Heo" is the word most Protestant Bible readers know from this story; a reviewer may choose "lợn" for the whole Bible.

decisions.choice: porcs (L, B); cochons (R)
decisions.reason: "Porc" is the usual word in careful French; Readable uses "cochon", the everyday word children know. The same in 5:12-16.

source.text: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And they begged him saying, Send us into the pigs, so that into them we may enter.

en.L: And they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter into them."
en.B: The spirits pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Send us over to the pigs. Let us go into them."
en.R: The evil spirits begged Jesus, "Let us go into the pigs! Send us into them!"

vi.L: Và chúng nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng: "Xin sai chúng tôi vào bầy heo, để chúng tôi nhập vào chúng."
vi.B: Các linh ấy nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Xin cho chúng tôi qua bầy heo kia, để chúng tôi nhập vào chúng."
vi.R: Các tà linh van xin Đức Giê-xu: "Xin cho chúng tôi nhập vào bầy heo! Xin sai chúng tôi vào chúng!"

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그분께 간청하며 말했다. "우리를 돼지들에게로 보내서, 우리가 그것들 속으로 들어가게 해 주십시오."
ko.B: 더러운 영들이 예수께 간청했다. "우리를 저 돼지들에게 보내 주십시오. 그 속으로 들어가게 해 주십시오."
ko.R: 악한 영들이 예수께 빌었다. "우리가 돼지들 속으로 들어가게 해 주십시오! 우리를 돼지들에게 보내 주십시오!"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaron, diciendo: «Envíanos a los cerdos, para que entremos en ellos».
es.B: Los espíritus {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaron: «Mándanos a los cerdos; déjanos entrar en ellos».
es.R: Los espíritus malignos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaron a Jesús: «¡Déjanos entrar en los cerdos! ¡Mándanos a ellos!».

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplièrent, disant : « Envoie-nous dans les porcs, afin que nous entrions en eux. »
fr.B: Les esprits {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplièrent : « Envoie-nous vers les porcs ; laisse-nous entrer en eux. »
fr.R: Les esprits mauvais ont supplié Jésus : « Laisse-nous aller dans les cochons ! Envoie-nous en eux ! »

sw.L: Nao wakamsihi, wakisema, "Tupeleke katika nguruwe, ili tuingie ndani yao."
sw.B: Roho hao wakamsihi, "Tupeleke kwa wale nguruwe; turuhusu tuingie ndani yao."
sw.R: Roho hao waovu wakamsihi Yesu, "Turuhusu tuingie ndani ya nguruwe! Tupeleke ndani yao!"

decisions.choice: they begged: the spirits, now in the plural
decisions.reason: The subject changes to the many spirits, who are named in 5:13.

decisions.choice: they begged him: without a named subject
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a subject, "all the demons". The shorter text, which the SBLGNT prints, is found in the earliest witnesses. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the spirits (B); the evil spirits (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since "they" could mean the people.

source.text: καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And he permitted them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} permitted them.
en.B: He gave them leave.
en.R: Jesus let them go.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho phép chúng.
vi.B: Ngài cho phép.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu cho chúng đi.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 허락하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 허락하셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그렇게 하라고 하셨다.

es.L: Y se lo permitió.
es.B: Jesús se lo permitió.
es.R: Jesús les dio permiso.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le leur permit.
fr.B: Il le leur permit.
fr.R: Jésus leur a permis d’y aller.

sw.L: Naye akawaruhusu.
sw.B: Akawapa ruhusa.
sw.R: Yesu akawaruhusu.

decisions.choice: he permitted: the spirits can act only with Jesus' leave
decisions.reason: The spirits ask; Jesus decides. Mark shows his authority over them (1:27).

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ὡς δισχίλιοι, καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out, the spirits the unclean entered into the pigs, and rushed the herd down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand, and they were drowning in the sea.

en.L: And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about 2,000 [of them], and they were drowned in the sea.
en.B: Out came the unclean spirits, and they went into the pigs. The whole herd, about 2,000 animals, stampeded down the steep slope into the lake and drowned there.
en.R: The evil spirits left the man and went into the pigs. Then the pigs ran wildly down the steep hill into the lake. There were about 2,000 pigs, and all of them drowned in the water.

vi.L: Và sau khi ra [khỏi người ấy], các linh ô uế nhập vào bầy heo, và cả bầy lao xuống dốc đứng, xuống biển, khoảng hai nghìn [con], và chúng chết đuối dưới biển.
vi.B: Các linh ô uế ra khỏi người ấy và nhập vào bầy heo. Cả bầy, khoảng hai nghìn con, lao xuống dốc đứng, nhào xuống biển và chết đuối ở đó.
vi.R: Các tà linh ra khỏi người ấy và nhập vào bầy heo. Cả bầy heo liền chạy ào xuống sườn đồi dốc đứng và lao xuống hồ. Có khoảng hai nghìn con heo, và tất cả đều chết đuối dưới nước.

ko.L: 그리고 더러운 영들이 나와서 돼지들 속으로 들어갔고, 그 떼가 비탈 아래로 바다를 향해 내달렸는데, [그 수가] 2,000마리쯤이었으며, 바다에서 빠져 죽어 갔다.
ko.B: 더러운 영들이 나와서 돼지들 속으로 들어갔다. 그러자 2,000마리쯤 되는 돼지 떼가 가파른 비탈을 내리달려 바다로 뛰어들어 빠져 죽었다.
ko.R: 악한 영들은 그 사람에게서 나와 돼지들 속으로 들어갔다. 그러자 돼지들이 미친 듯이 가파른 산비탈을 달려 내려가 호수로 뛰어들었다. 돼지는 2,000마리쯤 되었는데, 모두 물에 빠져 죽었다.

es.L: Y saliendo los espíritus impuros, entraron en los cerdos, y la piara se lanzó por el despeñadero al mar, unos 2000, y se ahogaban en el mar.
es.B: Los espíritus impuros salieron y entraron en los cerdos. Toda la piara, unos 2000 animales, se lanzó en estampida pendiente abajo hasta el mar, y allí se ahogaron.
es.R: Los espíritus malignos salieron del hombre y entraron en los cerdos. Entonces los cerdos corrieron como locos cuesta abajo y cayeron al lago. Eran unos 2000 cerdos, y todos se ahogaron en el agua.

fr.L: Et étant sortis, les esprits impurs entrèrent dans les porcs, et le troupeau, au nombre d’environ 2 000, se précipita du haut de l’escarpement dans la mer, et ils se noyaient dans la mer.
fr.B: Les esprits impurs sortirent et entrèrent dans les porcs. Tout le troupeau, environ 2 000 bêtes, s’élança du haut de la pente escarpée dans la mer, et ils s’y noyèrent.
fr.R: Les esprits mauvais sont sortis de l’homme et sont entrés dans les cochons. Alors les cochons se sont mis à courir comme des fous vers le bas de la colline, et ils sont tombés dans le lac. Il y avait environ 2 000 cochons, et ils se sont tous noyés.

sw.L: Na wakiisha kutoka, roho wachafu wakaingia katika nguruwe, na kundi likatimka mbio kuteremka mteremko mkali hadi baharini, wapata elfu mbili, nao wakawa wakizama baharini.
sw.B: Roho wachafu wakatoka, wakaingia ndani ya nguruwe. Kundi zima, nguruwe wapata elfu mbili, likatimka mbio kuteremka mteremko mkali, likaingia baharini, nao wakazama humo.
sw.R: Roho hao waovu wakamtoka yule mtu, wakaingia ndani ya nguruwe. Kisha nguruwe wakakimbia kwa nguvu kuteremka kilima kikali mpaka ziwani. Walikuwa nguruwe wapata elfu mbili, na wote wakazama majini.

decisions.choice: about two thousand: the size of the herd
decisions.reason: The number goes with the herd, and is the only number of animals Mark gives. It shows how many spirits had held the man.

decisions.choice: rushed: charged headlong
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a sudden violent rush.

decisions.choice: the spirits destroy what they enter
alternatives: Jesus wanted the pigs to drown
decisions.reason: What the spirits did to the pigs shows what they were doing to the man. The sea in Mark is also a place of chaos that Jesus rules (4:39-41).

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Balanced and Readable call the Sea of Galilee a lake, which it is.

decisions.choice: "hai nghìn" in words
decisions.reason: The style guide writes numbers in words in running text, where the English uses figures. "Nghìn" follows the Vietnamese John (6:10); a reviewer may prefer "ngàn" for the whole Bible.

decisions.choice: unos 2000
decisions.reason: Spanish writes four-digit numbers without a separator, as the Spanish of John does ("unos 5000").

decisions.choice: au nombre d’environ 2~000 (L); 2~000 in figures
decisions.reason: French cannot leave the number standing alone in the middle of the clause as the Greek does, so Literal says "au nombre de", as the French John does in 6:10; numbers above "cent" are written in figures with the French thin space.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς· καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός.

records.literal_gloss: And those feeding them fled and reported [it] in the city and in the fields; and they came to see what it is that has happened.

en.L: And those feeding them fled and reported [it] in the city and in the countryside, and [people] came to see what it was that had happened.
en.B: The men tending the pigs ran off and spread the news in the town and on the farms, and people came out to see what had taken place.
en.R: The men who took care of the pigs ran away. They told everyone in the town and on the farms what had happened. So people came out to see for themselves.

vi.L: Và những người chăn chúng bỏ chạy và báo tin trong thành và ở các vùng quê; và [người ta] đến xem việc đã xảy ra là gì.
vi.B: Những người chăn heo bỏ chạy, loan tin khắp trong thành và các làng quê, và dân chúng kéo đến xem việc gì đã xảy ra.
vi.R: Những người chăn heo bỏ chạy. Họ kể cho mọi người trong thành và ở các trang trại chung quanh biết việc đã xảy ra. Vì vậy, dân chúng kéo ra để tận mắt xem.

ko.L: 그리고 그것들을 치던 이들이 달아나서 성읍과 농촌에 알렸다. 그러자 [사람들이] 일어난 일이 무엇인지 보러 왔다.
ko.B: 돼지를 치던 사람들이 달아나서 읍내와 근처 농가들에 이 일을 알렸다. 그러자 사람들이 무슨 일이 일어났는지 보려고 나왔다.
ko.R: 돼지를 돌보던 사람들은 도망쳤다. 그들은 마을과 농촌에 사는 사람들에게 이 일을 모두 알렸다. 그래서 사람들이 직접 보려고 나왔다.

es.L: Y los que los apacentaban huyeron y [lo] contaron en la ciudad y en los campos; y [la gente] vino a ver qué era lo que había sucedido.
es.B: Los hombres que cuidaban los cerdos salieron huyendo y dieron la noticia en el pueblo y por los campos, y la gente salió a ver qué había pasado.
es.R: Los hombres que cuidaban los cerdos huyeron. Fueron al pueblo y a las granjas y les contaron a todos lo que había pasado. Entonces la gente salió a verlo con sus propios ojos.

fr.L: Et ceux qui les faisaient paître s’enfuirent et [le] rapportèrent dans la ville et dans les campagnes ; et [les gens] vinrent voir ce qui était arrivé.
fr.B: Les gardiens des porcs s’enfuirent et répandirent la nouvelle dans la ville et dans les fermes, et les gens vinrent voir ce qui s’était passé.
fr.R: Les hommes qui gardaient les cochons se sont enfuis. Ils ont raconté à tout le monde, dans la ville et dans les fermes, ce qui était arrivé. Alors les gens sont venus voir eux-mêmes.

sw.L: Na wale waliokuwa wakiwalisha wakakimbia, wakatoa habari mjini na mashambani; na [watu] wakaja kuona ni nini kilichotokea.
sw.B: Wachungaji wa nguruwe walikimbia, wakaeneza habari mjini na mashambani, na watu wakaja kuona yaliyokuwa yametokea.
sw.R: Watu waliokuwa wakichunga nguruwe hao walikimbia. Waliwaeleza watu wote mjini na mashambani yaliyotokea. Kwa hiyo watu wakaja kujionea wenyewe.

decisions.choice: the city and the fields: the town and the farms around it
decisions.reason: The word for city is used for towns of any size. "Fields" means the farmland and villages around.

decisions.choice: they came: the people who heard
decisions.reason: The subject is the people of the town and the countryside.

decisions.choice: told everyone ... what had happened
decisions.reason: Readable says what they reported.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα, τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to the Jesus and see the one being demon-possessed sitting, clothed and being of sound mind, the one having had the legion, and they were afraid.

en.L: And they come to Jesus and see the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind, the one who had had the legion, and they were afraid.
en.B: When they reached Jesus, they found the man the demons had held sitting there with clothes on and in his right mind, the very man who had been held by the legion. And they were afraid.
en.R: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had had all those demons. He was sitting there with his clothes on, and his mind was clear again. This made the people afraid.

vi.L: Và họ đến cùng Đức Giê-xu và thấy người bị quỷ ám đang ngồi, mặc áo và tỉnh trí, là người đã từng có cả quân đoàn ấy, và họ sợ hãi.
vi.B: Họ đến chỗ Đức Giê-xu và thấy người trước kia bị quỷ ám đang ngồi đó, mặc quần áo và tỉnh táo, chính là người đã bị cả quân đoàn quỷ ám. Họ đâm ra sợ hãi.
vi.R: Họ đến chỗ Đức Giê-xu và thấy người trước đây bị rất nhiều quỷ ám. Anh ta đang ngồi đó, có mặc quần áo, và đầu óc đã tỉnh táo lại. Thấy vậy, dân chúng sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 예수께 온다. 그리고 귀신 들린 사람, 곧 레기온이 들렸던 그 사람이 옷을 입고 제정신으로 앉아 있는 것을 본다. 그러자 그들은 두려워했다.
ko.B: 그들은 예수께 와서, 귀신 들렸던 사람, 레기온에게 사로잡혔던 바로 그 사람이 옷을 입고 멀쩡한 정신으로 앉아 있는 것을 보았다. 그러자 그들은 두려워졌다.
ko.R: 사람들이 예수께 왔다. 그들은 그 많은 귀신이 들어 있던 사람을 보았다. 그는 옷을 입고 앉아 있었다. 정신도 다시 맑아져 있었다. 그것을 보고 사람들은 무서워했다.

es.L: Y vienen adonde está Jesús, y ven al endemoniado sentado, vestido y en su sano juicio, al que había tenido la legión; y tuvieron miedo.
es.B: Cuando llegaron adonde estaba Jesús, encontraron sentado allí al hombre que había estado poseído por los demonios, vestido y en su sano juicio, el mismo que había tenido la legión. Y tuvieron miedo.
es.R: Llegaron adonde estaba Jesús y vieron al hombre que había tenido todos aquellos demonios. Estaba sentado allí, vestido, y otra vez podía pensar con claridad. Esto hizo que la gente tuviera miedo.

fr.L: Et ils viennent vers Jésus, et ils voient le démoniaque assis, vêtu et dans son bon sens, celui qui avait eu la légion, et ils eurent peur.
fr.B: Arrivés près de Jésus, ils virent l’homme qui avait été possédé par les démons, assis là, habillé et dans son bon sens, lui qui avait eu en lui la légion. Et ils furent saisis de crainte.
fr.R: Ils sont venus près de Jésus et ils ont vu l’homme qui avait eu tous ces démons. Il était assis là, il avait des vêtements, et il avait retrouvé la raison. Alors les gens ont eu peur.

sw.L: Nao wanakuja kwa Yesu, nao wanamwona yule aliyepagawa na pepo ameketi, amevaa nguo na ana akili timamu, yule aliyekuwa na Legioni, nao wakaogopa.
sw.B: Walipofika kwa Yesu, walimkuta yule mtu aliyekuwa amepagawa na pepo ameketi pale, amevaa nguo, na akili zake ziko timamu, yule yule aliyekuwa amepagawa na Legioni. Nao wakaogopa.
sw.R: Walifika kwa Yesu, wakamwona yule mtu aliyekuwa na pepo wale wote. Alikuwa ameketi pale, amevaa nguo, na akili zake zilikuwa zimerudi sawa. Jambo hili liliwaogopesha watu.

decisions.choice: the demon-possessed man: the one who had been possessed
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the description from before. The next words show that he is free now.

decisions.choice: clothed: he had gone without clothes before
decisions.reason: Mark does not say he was naked, but Luke 8:27 does. Being dressed is a sign of his return to normal life.

decisions.choice: of sound mind: sane, in control of himself
decisions.reason: The verb means to have a sound mind, the opposite of the raving he had shown (5:5).

decisions.choice: they were afraid: fear at a power beyond human control
decisions.reason: As the disciples feared after the storm (4:41), the people fear the one who has such power.

decisions.choice: they got to, they saw; they came, saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense for the storytelling present.

decisions.choice: "bị quỷ ám"
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese John (7:20; 10:20-21), "quỷ" renders the word for demon, and "bị quỷ ám" is the usual phrase for being possessed; "ma" would suggest the ghost of a dead person.

decisions.choice: "귀신 들린 사람" (L); "귀신 들렸던 사람" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "귀신" is the word for daimonion set in the Korean Mark 3:15. Literal keeps the Greek present participle ("the demon-possessed man") as Mark's name for him; Balanced and Readable make clear that he is possessed no longer (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: el endemoniado (L); el hombre que había estado poseído por los demonios (B)
decisions.reason: "Endemoniado" is the one Spanish word for the Greek participle. Balanced spells it out and shows that the possession is now past (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: le démoniaque (L); l’homme qui avait été possédé par les démons (B); l’homme qui avait eu tous ces démons (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the one being demon-possessed" though he is now free (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the single noun, "le démoniaque"; Balanced and Readable use the past so that no reader thinks he is still possessed.

decisions.choice: aliyepagawa na pepo (L, B); aliyekuwa na pepo (R)
decisions.reason: "Kupagawa na pepo" is the plain Swahili for being held by demons, and "pepo" is kept for Mark's word for demons, apart from "roho" for spirits (5:2). Readable says "had demons".

source.text: καὶ διηγήσαντο αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων.

records.literal_gloss: And described to them those having seen how it happened to the one being demon-possessed, and concerning the pigs.

en.L: And those who had seen [it] described to them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.
en.B: Those who had seen it all told them what had happened to the man with the demons, and about the pigs too.
en.R: The people who had seen everything told the others what had happened to the man. They also told them about the pigs.

vi.L: Và những người đã thấy [việc ấy] thuật lại cho họ việc đã xảy ra cho người bị quỷ ám thế nào, và về bầy heo.
vi.B: Những người đã chứng kiến kể lại cho họ mọi việc đã xảy ra cho người bị quỷ ám, và cả chuyện bầy heo nữa.
vi.R: Những người đã thấy tận mắt kể cho những người khác nghe việc đã xảy ra cho người ấy. Họ cũng kể về bầy heo.

ko.L: 그러자 본 사람들이 귀신 들린 사람에게 어떻게 [그 일이] 일어났는지, 그리고 돼지들에 관하여 그들에게 이야기했다.
ko.B: 그 일을 본 사람들이 귀신 들렸던 사람에게 일어난 일과 돼지들에 관한 일을 그들에게 자세히 이야기해 주었다.
ko.R: 모든 것을 본 사람들이 다른 사람들에게 그 사람에게 일어난 일을 말해 주었다. 돼지들에게 일어난 일도 말해 주었다.

es.L: Y los que [lo] habían visto les contaron cómo le había sucedido al endemoniado, y lo de los cerdos.
es.B: Los que lo habían visto todo les contaron lo que le había pasado al endemoniado, y también lo de los cerdos.
es.R: Los que habían visto todo les contaron a los demás lo que le había pasado al hombre. También les contaron lo que pasó con los cerdos.

fr.L: Et ceux qui avaient vu leur racontèrent comment cela était arrivé au démoniaque, et [ce qui concernait] les porcs.
fr.B: Ceux qui avaient tout vu leur racontèrent ce qui était arrivé à l’homme possédé par les démons, et aussi ce qui était arrivé aux porcs.
fr.R: Ceux qui avaient tout vu ont raconté aux autres ce qui était arrivé à l’homme. Ils ont aussi parlé des cochons.

sw.L: Na wale walioona wakawasimulia jinsi ilivyompata yule aliyepagawa na pepo, na habari za nguruwe.
sw.B: Wale walioyaona yote wakawaeleza yaliyompata yule mtu aliyekuwa na pepo, na pia habari za nguruwe.
sw.R: Watu walioona kila kitu wakawaeleza wengine yaliyompata yule mtu. Wakawaeleza pia habari za nguruwe.

decisions.choice: those who had seen: the herdsmen and other witnesses
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were, only that they had seen it.

decisions.choice: and about the pigs: the loss of the herd is part of the report
decisions.reason: The people hear of both the man's cure and their loss, which leads to their request (5:17).

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And they began to beg him to depart from the region of them.

en.L: And they began to beg {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to depart from their region.
en.B: Then they started pleading with Jesus to go away from their district.
en.R: Then the people begged Jesus to leave their land.

vi.L: Và họ bắt đầu nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi địa phận của họ.
vi.B: Bấy giờ họ bắt đầu nài nỉ Đức Giê-xu rời khỏi vùng của họ.
vi.R: Rồi dân chúng xin Đức Giê-xu rời khỏi xứ của họ.

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 자기들 지역에서 떠나 달라고 그분께 간청하기 시작했다.
ko.B: 그러자 사람들은 자기네 지방에서 떠나 달라고 예수께 간청하기 시작했다.
ko.R: 그러자 사람들은 자기들 땅에서 떠나 달라고 예수께 빌었다.

es.L: Y comenzaron a rogarle que se fuera de su región.
es.B: Entonces comenzaron a suplicarle a Jesús que se marchara de su territorio.
es.R: Entonces la gente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidió a Jesús que se fuera de su tierra.

fr.L: Et ils commencèrent à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplier de s’en aller de leur territoire.
fr.B: Alors ils se mirent à supplier Jésus de quitter leur région.
fr.R: Alors les gens ont supplié Jésus de quitter leur pays.

sw.L: Nao wakaanza kumsihi aondoke katika mipaka yao.
sw.B: Kisha wakaanza kumsihi Yesu aondoke katika eneo lao.
sw.R: Basi watu wakamsihi Yesu aondoke katika nchi yao.

decisions.choice: they began to beg: the people of the region
decisions.reason: Those who came out to see now ask Jesus to leave.

decisions.choice: to depart from their region: they would rather lose Jesus than face his power
alternatives: they were only angry about the pigs
decisions.reason: Mark gives no reason. Their fear (5:15) and their loss (5:16) are both in view.

source.text: καὶ ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα μετ’ αὐτοῦ ᾖ.

records.literal_gloss: And getting in of him into the boat, was begging him the one having been demon-possessed that with him he might be.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that he might be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: As Jesus stepped into the boat, the man freed from the demons pleaded to go along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was stepping into the boat. Then the man who used to have the demons begged Jesus, "Please let me go with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang bước lên thuyền, người đã từng bị quỷ ám nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho được ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu bước lên thuyền, người được giải thoát khỏi quỷ nài xin được đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Lúc Đức Giê-xu đang bước lên thuyền, người trước kia bị quỷ ám van xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Xin cho tôi đi theo Thầy!"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 배에 오르실 때에, 귀신 들렸던 사람이 그분과 함께 있게 해 달라고 그분께 간청하고 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 배에 오르실 때에, 귀신에게서 풀려난 그 사람이 자기도 함께 가게 해 달라고 간청했다.
ko.R: 예수께서 배에 오르고 계셨다. 그때 전에 귀신이 들렸던 그 사람이 예수께 간청했다. "저도 함께 가게 해 주십시오!"

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} subía a la barca, el que había estado endemoniado {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba que [lo dejara] estar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Cuando Jesús subía a la barca, el hombre que había sido liberado de los demonios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicó que lo dejara ir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús estaba subiendo a la barca. Entonces el hombre que antes tenía los demonios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogó: «¡Por favor, déjame ir contigo!».

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} montait dans la barque, celui qui avait été démoniaque {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliait de pouvoir être avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Comme Jésus montait dans la barque, l’homme délivré des démons {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplia de pouvoir partir avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus montait dans la barque. Alors l’homme qui avait eu les démons {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a supplié : « Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, laisse-moi partir avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ! »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akipanda mashuani, yule aliyekuwa amepagawa na pepo alikuwa akimsihi ili awe pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akipanda mashua, yule mtu aliyeachiliwa kutoka kwa pepo alimsihi amruhusu aende pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akipanda mashua, yule mtu aliyekuwa na pepo zamani alimsihi Yesu, "Tafadhali, niruhusu niende pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}!"

decisions.choice: that he might be with him: to go with Jesus as a disciple
decisions.reason: "To be with him" is the phrase Mark used for the Twelve (3:14). The man asks to join those who follow Jesus.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Please let me go with you!
alternatives: that he might be with him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" in the man's words (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech, as the English does. The man asks to go with Jesus as a disciple (meaning decision), so he calls him "Thầy", the word disciples use; it is a noun of address and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: contigo, without a setting span
decisions.reason: By the rule for Mark set at 1:2, "conmigo", "contigo" and "consigo" are written plain; the separate pronouns for Jesus in this sentence ("le", "él") take the setting.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς, καὶ ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ὁ κύριός σοι πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And not he permitted him, but he says to him, Go to the home of you, to the your own, and report to them how much the Lord for you has done, and had mercy on you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not permit him, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Go to your home, to your own [people], and report to them how much the Lord has done for you, and [how] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had mercy on you."
en.B: But Jesus would not let him, and told him instead, "Go home to your own people, and let them know all that the Lord has done for you, and the mercy {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown you."
en.R: But Jesus did not let him come. Jesus told him, "Go home to your family. Tell them all that the Lord has done for you. Tell them how kind {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been to you."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không cho phép anh ta, nhưng nói với anh ta: "Hãy về nhà anh, đến với người nhà của anh, và thuật lại cho họ mọi điều Chúa đã làm cho anh, và [thể nào] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã thương xót anh."
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không cho, mà bảo anh ta: "Hãy về nhà với người thân của anh, và kể cho họ biết mọi điều Chúa đã làm cho anh, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã thương xót anh thế nào."
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không cho anh ta đi theo. Ngài bảo anh ta: "Hãy về nhà với gia đình anh. Hãy kể cho họ nghe mọi điều Chúa đã làm cho anh. Hãy cho họ biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã thương xót anh biết bao."

ko.L: 그러나 그분은 그를 허락하지 않으시고, 그에게 말씀하신다. "네 집으로, 네 사람들에게 가서, 주님께서 너에게 얼마나 큰일을 하셨는지, 그리고 [어떻게] 너를 불쌍히 여기셨는지 그들에게 알려라."
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 허락하지 않으시고 그에게 말씀하셨다. "집으로 네 가족에게 돌아가서, 주님께서 너에게 하신 모든 일과 너에게 베푸신 자비를 그들에게 알려라."
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 그가 따라오지 못하게 하셨다. 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "집으로 가족에게 돌아가거라. 주님께서 너에게 해 주신 모든 일을 그들에게 이야기해라. 주님께서 너를 얼마나 불쌍히 여겨 주셨는지 말해 주어라."

es.L: Y no se lo permitió, sino que le dice: «Vete a tu casa, a los tuyos, y cuéntales cuánto ha hecho el Señor por ti, y [cómo] tuvo misericordia de ti».
es.B: Pero Jesús no se lo permitió, sino que le dijo: «Vete a tu casa, con tu gente, y cuéntales todo lo que el Señor ha hecho por ti y la misericordia que ha tenido contigo».
es.R: Pero Jesús no lo dejó ir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Le dijo: «Vete a tu casa, con tu familia. Cuéntales todo lo que el Señor ha hecho por ti. Cuéntales lo bueno que ha sido contigo».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne le lui permit pas, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Va dans ta maison, vers les tiens, et rapporte-leur tout ce que le Seigneur a fait pour toi, et [comment] {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a eu pitié de toi. »
fr.B: Mais Jésus refusa et lui dit : « Rentre chez toi, auprès des tiens, et fais-leur savoir tout ce que le Seigneur a fait pour toi, et comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a eu pitié de toi. »
fr.R: Mais Jésus ne l’a pas laissé venir. Il lui a dit : « Rentre chez toi, dans ta famille. Raconte-leur tout ce que le Seigneur a fait pour toi. Dis-leur combien {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été bon pour toi. »

sw.L: Lakini hakumruhusu, bali anamwambia, "Nenda nyumbani kwako kwa watu wako, ukawaeleze ni mambo mangapi Bwana amekutendea, na [jinsi] alivyokuhurumia."
sw.B: Lakini Yesu hakumruhusu, bali alimwambia, "Nenda nyumbani kwa watu wako, ukawajulishe yote ambayo Bwana amekutendea, na jinsi alivyokuonea huruma."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakumruhusu aje. Akamwambia, "Nenda nyumbani kwa jamaa zako. Waeleze yote ambayo Bwana amekutendea. Waeleze jinsi alivyokuwa mwema kwako."

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: Jesus points to God as the one who has acted. In 5:20 the man tells what Jesus did: in Jesus, God has acted.

decisions.choice: go and report: here Jesus sends the man to tell
alternatives: Jesus breaks his own rule of silence
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Jesus forbids people to tell (1:44; 5:43). In Gentile country, away from the crowds of Galilee, he sends this man home to tell what God has done.

decisions.choice: your own: your family and people
decisions.reason: The phrase means those who belong to him: his household and relatives.

decisions.choice: had mercy: showed pity and acted to help
decisions.reason: The verb is used for the pity that moves someone to help (10:47-48).

decisions.choice: how kind he has been to you
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for mercy.

decisions.choice: "thương xót" at every level
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "how kind he has been"; Vietnamese "thương xót" (have pity and help) is an everyday word, so Readable keeps it with "biết bao" (how much).

decisions.choice: "주님께서" for the Lord (God); "불쌍히 여기다" (L, R), "자비를 베풀다" (B) for had mercy
decisions.reason: "The Lord" here is God (meaning decision); Korean "주님" with the honorific keeps Mark's word without naming him further. "긍휼" is an older church word; "불쌍히 여기다" says pity that acts, and Balanced uses "자비" for the mercy shown.

decisions.choice: tuvo misericordia (L); la misericordia que ha tenido (B); lo bueno que ha sido (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the word for mercy, pity that acts to help (meaning decision); Readable says it in everyday words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: le Seigneur, with {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} for God
decisions.reason: "The Lord" here is God (meaning decision m1), so the pronoun that follows takes the deity_pronoun setting, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον.

records.literal_gloss: And he departed and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much did for him the Jesus, and all were marveling.

en.L: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
en.B: So he went off and started to tell all through the Decapolis the great things Jesus had done for him. Everyone who heard was astonished.
en.R: So the man left. He went through the area called the Ten Towns, the Decapolis, and told people how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.

vi.L: Và anh ta ra đi và bắt đầu rao truyền trong vùng Đê-ca-bô-lơ mọi điều Đức Giê-xu đã làm cho mình, và mọi người đều kinh ngạc.
vi.B: Vậy anh ta ra đi, và bắt đầu rao truyền khắp vùng Đê-ca-bô-lơ những việc lớn Đức Giê-xu đã làm cho mình. Ai nghe cũng đều kinh ngạc.
vi.R: Vậy người ấy ra đi. Anh ta đi khắp vùng Mười Thành, tức là Đê-ca-bô-lơ, và kể cho mọi người nghe Đức Giê-xu đã làm cho mình biết bao nhiêu điều. Ai cũng ngạc nhiên.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 떠나가서, 예수께서 자기에게 얼마나 큰일을 하셨는지 데가볼리에서 선포하기 시작했다. 그러자 모두가 놀라워하고 있었다.
ko.B: 그는 떠나가서, 예수께서 자기에게 하신 큰일을 데가볼리 온 지역에 선포하기 시작했다. 그 말을 들은 사람은 모두 놀랐다.
ko.R: 그래서 그 사람은 떠나갔다. 그는 '열 도시'라는 뜻의 데가볼리 지방을 다니며, 예수께서 자기에게 해 주신 일을 사람들에게 이야기했다. 모든 사람이 놀랐다.

es.L: Y se fue y comenzó a proclamar en la Decápolis cuánto había hecho Jesús por él; y todos se maravillaban.
es.B: Así que se fue y comenzó a contar por toda la Decápolis las grandes cosas que Jesús había hecho por él. Todos los que lo oían quedaban asombrados.
es.R: Entonces el hombre se fue. Recorrió la región de las Diez Ciudades, llamada la Decápolis, y contaba a la gente todo lo que Jesús había hecho por él. Todos se quedaban asombrados.

fr.L: Et il s’en alla et commença à proclamer dans la Décapole tout ce que Jésus avait fait pour lui ; et tous étaient dans l’étonnement.
fr.B: Il partit donc et se mit à proclamer dans toute la Décapole ce que Jésus avait fait pour lui. Et tous ceux qui l’entendaient étaient émerveillés.
fr.R: L’homme est donc parti. Il est allé dans la région des Dix Villes, la Décapole, et il racontait à tout le monde tout ce que Jésus avait fait pour lui. Et tout le monde était très étonné.

sw.L: Naye akaenda zake, akaanza kutangaza katika Dekapoli mambo yote ambayo Yesu alimtendea; nao wote wakashangaa.
sw.B: Basi akaenda zake, akaanza kutangaza katika Dekapoli yote mambo makuu ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemtendea. Kila aliyesikia alishangaa.
sw.R: Basi mtu huyo akaondoka. Alipita katika eneo liitwalo Miji Kumi, yaani Dekapoli, akiwaeleza watu yote ambayo Yesu alimtendea. Watu wote walishangaa.

decisions.choice: the Decapolis: a league of ten Greek cities, mostly east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The name means Ten Cities. They were Gentile cities of Greek culture, including Gerasa and Gadara.

decisions.choice: proclaim: announce publicly
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same verb for John, Jesus and the disciples (1:4, 14; 3:14). The healed man becomes a herald.

decisions.choice: how much Jesus had done: told to report what the Lord did (5:19), he tells what Jesus did
